text:
Emma: :rotating_light: incident-bot just opened a burn-rate alert for SLO 'request-success-rate' — multi-window windows are spiking across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Looks like automated retries + a regression in the batching path. Paging fired due to our current high-severity criteria. I'm on it and starting a handoff.
IncidentBot: [AUTO] Alert: slo.burn_rate_high | scope: production | regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1 | count: 4 distinct services | severity: HIGH | link: https://redwood.ops/alerts/2111112233
Emma: quick plan: 1) confirm customer impact 2) triage service causing highest burn 3) short-term tuning to avoid pager spam if this is noisy 4) create dashboard + followup for proper tuning.
Raj: I'm seeing a surge of 429/5xx from the gateway when retry loops are active. Top offender is batch-worker-v2. Rolling back the last deploy (sha a1b2c3) is an option if needed. Logs show repeated attempts in ~30s windows.
Li: I can throw a narrow suppress for the low-severity burn alerts (non-paging) but keep the high-severity pages. Propose: suppress alerts for single-window spikes < 2min but keep multi-window sustained conditions.
Maya: agree. current paging rule is too eager for transient retry storms. Suggest adjusting the paging rule to require sustained burn across 3 of 5 windows before paging. That would still page for persistent outages but cut noise.
Ben: tagging the policy proposal here. Current rule (pseudo):
```
alert: slo_burn_high_pager
when: burn_rate{window="1m"} > 2.0
for: 1m
page: true
```
Proposed tweak:
```
alert: slo_burn_high_pager_multiwindow
when: burn_rate_multiwindow(windows=5, threshold=1.5) >= 3
for: 0m
page: true
```
This means at least 3 windows out of 5 exceed threshold => page. Cuts single-window flares. Thoughts?
Sam: from support POV we need quick customer impact assessment — how many active customers saw errors vs degraded latency? If it's mostly retries internal to workers (no customer-facing 500s) we can be less aggressive. Please post counts.
Raj: quick numbers from logs (approx): unique customer API keys with errors in last 10m = 12, 500s = 3, elevated latencies (>1.5s) = 120. So some customers degraded.
Emma: thanks. Given customer visible impact, leave current paging open for now while we act. Steps: A) temporary guardrail: update alert to multi-window rule but keep immediate pages for systems with >5% customer error rate; B) trigger rollback of batch-worker-v2 if errors don't drop in 5m; C) create runbook entry.
Li: I've drafted a short-lived suppression rule to mute non-pager SLO burn alerts for 10m for services in deployment flaps. Applying now: suppress-id=tmp-suppress-211111.
IncidentBot: [AUTO] Suppression applied: tmp-suppress-211111 by Li — expires in 10m.
Maya: I'll start building the temporary dashboard panel that shows: burn-rate (1m/5m/15m), customer-error-rate, top 5 services by token/sec, and retry count. Link will be posted when ready.
Ben: creating a ticket for follow-up alert tuning + dashboard cleanup: RD-INT-1023. Will document suggested thresholds and run the simulation against last two incidents.
Sam: I'll notify CS and a small cohort of affected customers (those with errors) with a brief note and ETA. Keep me updated on rollback decision.
Emma: rollback queued (manual) if error-rate doesn't drop under 1% for the next 5m. Also capturing decision: we'll transition to proposed multi-window paging rule permanently if this incident shows mostly retry noise.
Raj: after disabling the faulty retry logic in gateway (hotfix), I see error counts dropping — 500s down to 1, latencies trending down. Looks promising.
Li: suppress-expired in 4m — will extend if noise continues.
Maya: dashboard live: https://redwood.ops/dashboards/211111-burn-watch — contains the panels we discussed.
Ben: post-incident action items: - validate new paging rule in staging - run historical simulation against last 30 days - update runbooks + add the 'customer-error-rate' gate to paging criteria - schedule alert review meeting next Tue.
Emma: agreed. Closing loop: if metrics continue to improve we'll close the page and mark incident as 'mitigated, followup required'. If not, escalate rollback.
Sam: :thumbsup: I'll send the customer note now.
IncidentBot: [AUTO] Page resolved for alert slo.burn_rate_high at 2111112297. Incident status: mitigated. Followup ticket: RD-INT-1023.
Emma: Great job team. Postmortem: include timeline, the suppression decision, the new multi-window rule, and when we flip it to default. I'll own the post-incident doc.
Raj: adding a small log sample of the retry loop for the postmortem:
```
[2026-03-14T14:33:12Z] gateway batch request id=xxxx attempts=6 status=429
[2026-03-14T14:33:42Z] gateway batch request id=xxxx attempts=7 status=429
```
Maya: noted. I'll add the dashboard snapshots to the postmortem.
Li: extending suppression another 10m to avoid chatter while we tune. tmp-suppress-211111 extended by Li.
Ben: filing the alert rule PR now. Will include test harness and simulation results.
Emma: thanks all. Closing thread when postmortem is up. :wave:
